label: early-position steps (t=2..4) shortly after a t at the start of the sequence
explanation: Fires during the original-input phase at steps 2-5 (peak at t=3, nearly all mass at t=2..4) when the token t appeared at position 0 (first_tok=t: 21x lift, 84% of mass) or, more weakly, at position 1. Which token is currently being input does not matter. Magnitude is largest when the sequence starts with repeated t (t t t ...), peaks at step 3 or 4, and drops off by step 5-6. Activations are weaker when t is at position 1 instead of position 0, and many of those steps are false positives. Almost silent at t=0,1, at t>=6, in the copy phase, and when t first appears later in the sequence; it fires weakly at the delimiter for short sequences that start with t.

issues: The orig(1)==t branch has a systematic precision gap, not scattered noise. On dev, (phase==0)&(t in 3..4)&(orig(1)==t)&(orig(0)!=t) has precision 0.69 and carries only 15.5% of activation mass. Split by first token, precision is close to zero when orig(0) is in {b,d,f,h,l,n,0}: b 0.010, d 0.082, f 0.018, h 0.000, l 0.000, n 0.043, 0 0.015. It is middling for a 0.64, i 0.55, 1 0.65, q 0.80 and r 0.69, and 0.92-1.00 for nearly every other first token. Test false positives are mostly of the form 'n t ...', '0 t ...', 'd t ...', 'f t ...'. The explanation only says 'many of those steps are false positives' and does not name this token dependence.

The orig(0)==t branch alone (t=2..4, phase 0) has precision 0.984 and 80% of mass, so it supports the main claim. Recall is only 0.62 by count, though, so the position-1 branch is not minor by step count.

The step 5 tail is real but weak: (phase==0)&(t==5)&(orig(0)==t) has precision 0.33 and 2.3% of mass. Calling t=5 part of the firing range (as the explanation does with 'steps 2-5') slightly overclaims; leaving it out of the predicate is correct.

Checked and confirmed: silent at t=0 and t=1 (0 active steps); about 0 at t>=7; copy phase holds 0.1% of mass; the delimiter step holds 1.5% of mass (most of it on output t); in_tok lift is flat at about 1.1x for all tokens, so the current input token really does not matter.
Adding the first-token exclusion to the orig(1) branch raises test precision from 0.874 to 0.958 and leaves recall unchanged (0.887 vs 0.889). That confirms the gap is systematic.
